definition: The list of investment strategies a fund can follow, as the sponsor's investors and regulators describe them. The chief financial officer of the funds decides what goes on it. It is not a classification of industries.

values.name: Growth
values.definition: Takes minority or control stakes in growing companies.

values.name: Secondaries
values.definition: Buys existing interests in funds or assets.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types (72): none lists fund strategies. Instrument and industry lists describe other things.

definition: The list of ways a holder relates to a company in which it has a stake: control, joint control, significant influence or a minority holding. The head of portfolio management decides what goes on it. It sits alongside the list LegalEntityRelationshipTypes and does not repeat it.

values.name: Control
values.definition: The holder directs the company on its own.

values.name: Joint Control
values.definition: The holder directs the company together with others.

values.name: Significant Influence
values.definition: The holder influences the company without directing it.

values.name: Minority
values.definition: A passive holding with no influence.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: LegalEntityRelationshipTypes DLT000000061 holds Parent and Minority but states it is superseded by relationship records.

definition: The list of kinds of vehicle that invest alongside a fund: a parallel fund, an alternative investment vehicle and a co-investment vehicle. The general counsel decides what goes on it.

values.name: Parallel Fund
values.definition: Invests side by side with the main fund on the same terms.

values.name: Alternative Investment Vehicle
values.definition: Takes an investment the main fund cannot hold directly.

values.name: Co-investment Vehicle
values.definition: Lets selected investors take a further share of one investment.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: none lists side-by-side vehicle kinds.

definition: The list of kinds of transaction in the fund structure: capital call, distribution, acquisition, follow-on investment, partial exit, full exit and transfer to a continuation vehicle. The chief financial officer of the funds decides what goes on it.

values.name: Capital Call
values.definition: Investors pay money into a fund.

values.name: Distribution
values.definition: A fund pays money to its investors.

values.name: Acquisition
values.definition: A fund buys its first holding in a company.

values.name: Follow-on Investment
values.definition: A fund adds to an existing holding.

values.name: Partial Exit
values.definition: A fund sells part of a holding.

values.name: Full Exit
values.definition: A fund sells all of a holding.

values.name: Continuation Transfer
values.definition: A holding moves from one fund to a continuation vehicle.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: only instrument date and trading status lists exist; none lists transaction kinds.

definition: The list of purposes for which an amount is paid or received in a transaction: investment, management fee, fund expense, return of capital, realised gain, income, and recallable amount. The chief financial officer of the funds decides what goes on it.

values.name: Investment
values.definition: Money used to buy a holding.

values.name: Management Fee
values.definition: Money used to pay the manager.

values.name: Fund Expense
values.definition: Money used to pay the fund's costs.

values.name: Realised Gain
values.definition: Money that is a gain on a sale.

values.name: Income
values.definition: Money received as dividends or interest.

values.name: Recallable Amount
values.definition: Money that the fund may call again.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: none lists purposes of a payment.

definition: The three levels of the fair value hierarchy: Level 1 uses quoted prices, Level 2 uses other observable inputs, Level 3 uses unobservable inputs. The head of portfolio valuation decides what goes on it.

values.name: Level 1
values.definition: Quoted prices in active markets for the same instrument.

values.name: Level 2
values.definition: Other inputs observable for the instrument.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: none holds a fair value hierarchy.

definition: The list of kinds of price held for an instrument: a closing price and a fair value assessed at a reporting date. The head of portfolio valuation decides what goes on it.

values.name: Closing Price
values.definition: The last price of a trading day.

values.name: Fair Value
values.definition: The value assessed at a reporting date.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: InstrumentPriceType has no lookup bound to it.

definition: The list of measures on which a legal entity is valued: net asset value, equity value and enterprise value. The head of portfolio valuation decides what goes on it.

values.name: Net Asset Value
values.definition: The value of a fund's assets less its liabilities.

values.name: Equity Value
values.definition: The value of the owners' interest in a company or vehicle.

values.name: Enterprise Value
values.definition: The value of the whole business, being the owners' interest plus net debt.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: DLT000000063 holds market-value variants only; a list naming the measure of value is created for Valuation and DLT000000063 is left as it is.

definition: The most detailed level of the list of classifications applied to a legal entity. Here it carries what a vehicle is for. The general counsel decides the vehicle purposes on it.

values.name: Management Company
values.definition: Employs the people who manage the funds.

values.name: Special Purpose Vehicle
values.definition: Set up to hold one investment.

values.name: Tax Blocker
values.definition: A corporate vehicle through which an investor holds an investment.

values.name: Fund Vehicle
values.definition: A pooled vehicle managed for investors.

reuse_search: Searched DDA lookup types: DLT000000052 to DLT000000054 hold no values; vehicle purposes are added at the most detailed level.

definition: The list of kinds of commitment an investor makes to a fund, such as primary, secondary, general partner commitment and continuation vehicle. The head of investor relations decides what goes on it.

values.name: Primary
values.definition: A commitment made directly to the fund.

values.name: Secondary
values.definition: A commitment from buying an existing investor's interest.

values.name: GP Commitment
values.definition: Capital committed by the general partner or its principals.

values.name: Recycled
values.definition: Returned capital recalled by the fund.

values.name: Stapled
values.definition: A commitment required for access to another fund.

values.name: Continuation Vehicle
values.definition: A commitment to a continuation fund.

definition: The list of schemes and authorities under which a legal entity is identified, such as the legal entity identifier, a company registration number or a tax number. The head of compliance decides what goes on it.

values.name: CIK

values.name: EIN

values.name: UKCH

definition: The list saying which side of a transaction a party was on: it paid or it received. The chief financial officer of the funds decides what goes on it.

values.name: Paid
values.definition: The party gave money, and received the holding if there was one.

values.name: Received
values.definition: The party took money, and gave up the holding if there was one.
